url.invalid: This is not a valid URL. Check the highlighted part.
url.too-long: The URL is longer than the 32,000-character limit.
url.unsupported-scheme: This tool only works with http and https links.
host.invalid: This is not a valid host name or URL.
dns.ip-literal: This is an IP address: there is no name to look up in DNS.
dns.special-use: This is a special-use name (such as localhost or .local) that does not exist in public DNS.
inspect.blocked: Blocked for security: we do not follow links to internal destinations.
inspect.blocked.private-address: Blocked: the destination is a private, local or metadata address.
inspect.blocked.scheme: Blocked: only http and https links are followed.
inspect.blocked.credentials: Blocked: the link includes a username or password.
inspect.blocked.port: Blocked: only ports 80, 443, 8080 and 8443 are allowed.
inspect.blocked.unresolvable: The domain could not be found (it has no address).
inspect.timeout: The destination took too long to respond.
inspect.tls: The destination's security certificate is not valid.
inspect.network: Could not connect to the destination.
inspect.invalid-location: The destination redirects to an address that is not valid.
input.multiple-urls: There were several URLs; only the first one was used.
input.scheme-assumed: It had no scheme; https:// was assumed.
parse.warning.backslash: It contains backslashes (\). Browsers read them as normal slashes, but other programs may not.
parse.warning.control-chars: It contained line breaks or tabs, which were removed.
parse.warning.numeric-ipv4: The IP address is written in an unusual form; browsers read it as {host}.
parse.warning.invalid-encoding: It has invalid percent-encoding (a % not followed by two valid digits).
parse.warning.non-special-scheme: With this scheme, different programs may read the URL differently.
clean.reason.campaign: Identifies the marketing campaign you came from.
clean.reason.ad-click: Identifies your click on an ad so the ad platform can attribute it.
clean.reason.email: Identifies the email and the person who opened it.
clean.reason.analytics: Used to link your visit across analytics tools.
clean.reason.social: Records who shared the link or where from.
clean.reason.affiliate: Affiliate or referral marker; it does not change the content.
clean.reason.wrapper: It was a {platform} redirect; the real destination has been extracted.
clean.reason.canonical: Equivalent short form of the product link.
explain.part.scheme.https: https: the connection to the site is encrypted.
explain.part.scheme.http: http: the connection is not encrypted; others on the network could see it.
explain.part.scheme.dangerous: {scheme}: it does not open a web page; it can run code or show embedded content.
explain.part.scheme.other: {scheme}: not a web page; another app opens it.
explain.part.userinfo: Embedded username or password. They are not part of the site you are going to.
explain.part.host: The server the browser connects to.
explain.part.registrable-domain: The real site: whoever controls this domain controls the page.
explain.part.subdomain: Subdomain: a section chosen by the owner of {domain}.
explain.part.port: Port {port}: a "door" other than the server's usual one.
explain.part.path: The path: which page or resource is requested within the site.
explain.part.param.tracking: {name}: a {platform} tracking parameter. It does not change the content.
explain.part.param.functional: {name}: a parameter the site may use to show the content.
explain.part.fragment: The fragment: a position within the page. It is not sent to the server.
explain.signal.userinfo-deception: What comes before @ ({shown}) is not the destination. The real site is {real}.
explain.signal.ip-host: The destination is an IP address instead of a domain name.
explain.signal.homograph: The domain uses letters from another alphabet that look Latin. Its real form is {ascii}.
explain.signal.mixed-scripts: The domain mixes different alphabets. Its real form is {ascii}.
explain.signal.excessive-encoding: It has a lot of percent-encoding, which can hide what it really says.
explain.signal.double-encoding: It is double-encoded (%25…), a common way to hide content.
explain.signal.dangerous-scheme: The {scheme} scheme can run code or show content without opening a website.
explain.signal.unusual-port: It uses port {port}, which is unusual for public sites.
explain.signal.abuse-tld: The domain ends in .{tld}, an ending often used in abuse campaigns. It does not mean this site is one.
headers.hsts.missing: Strict-Transport-Security is missing: the browser is not told to always use https for this site.
headers.hsts.short-max-age: Strict-Transport-Security lasts {maxAge} s; at least {min} s (one year) is recommended.
headers.hsts.invalid: Strict-Transport-Security has no valid max-age, so the browser ignores it.
headers.csp.missing: Content-Security-Policy is missing: nothing limits which scripts the page may run.
headers.csp.report-only: There is only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: it reports problems but blocks nothing.
headers.csp.unsafe-inline: The policy allows inline scripts ('unsafe-inline'), which is what an XSS attack relies on.
headers.csp.unsafe-eval: The policy allows 'unsafe-eval': the page can run text as code.
headers.csp.unsafe-source: The policy accepts scripts from {source}, a source that is too broad.
headers.csp.no-script-restriction: The policy has no script-src or default-src, so it does not limit scripts.
headers.framing.missing: Nothing stops another site from showing this page inside a frame (frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options is missing).
headers.framing.invalid: X-Frame-Options has a value browsers do not recognise, so it does not protect.
headers.nosniff.missing: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is missing; the browser may guess a file's type.
headers.nosniff.invalid: X-Content-Type-Options only accepts the value nosniff.
headers.referrer.missing: Referrer-Policy is missing: the browser's default policy applies.
headers.referrer.unsafe-url: Referrer-Policy is unsafe-url: the full address, query included, is sent to every linked site.
headers.referrer.invalid: Referrer-Policy has no valid value, so the browser ignores it.
headers.permissions.missing: Permissions-Policy is missing: access to camera, microphone, location, etc. is not restricted.
headers.cookie.not-secure: Cookie {name} has no Secure flag: it would also travel over unencrypted http.
headers.cookie.not-httponly: Cookie {name} has no HttpOnly flag: the page's scripts can read it.
headers.cookie.samesite-none-insecure: Cookie {name} uses SameSite=None without Secure: browsers reject it.
metadata.missing-title: The page declares no title: the preview will show the address or nothing.
metadata.missing-description: The page declares no description for the preview.
metadata.missing-image: There is no preview image (og:image): the link will be shared without an image.
metadata.canonical-cross-domain: The canonical URL points to another site ({canonical}): search engines may credit it with the content.
metadata.image-relative: og:image is a relative address; the Open Graph protocol requires an absolute one and some networks will not show it.
metadata.truncated: The document is larger than 1 MiB: only the first MiB was analyzed.
metadata.not-html: The response is not an HTML page ({type}): there is no metadata to extract.
metadata.unknown-encoding: The page declares an unknown encoding ({label}); it was read as windows-1252.
tls.expired: The certificate expired on {date}: browsers show an error when visiting.
tls.not-yet-valid: The certificate is not valid yet: it starts on {date}.
tls.self-signed: The certificate is self-signed: no authority browsers recognise vouches for it.
tls.name-mismatch: The certificate is not for this name: browsers reject it.
tls.incomplete-chain: An intermediate certificate is missing from the chain: some browsers and programs cannot verify it.
tls.untrusted-root: The chain does not end in a trusted authority ({reason}).
tls.weak-signature: The chain uses a weak signature ({algorithm}), no longer considered secure.
tls.legacy-protocol: The server negotiates {protocol}, an obsolete protocol version.
tls.timeout: The server took too long to answer the secure connection.
tls.refused: The server refused the connection on that port.
tls.no-tls: That port does not speak TLS: the site offers no secure connection there.
tls.handshake-failed: The secure connection with the server could not be completed.
dns.unavailable: The DNS resolvers are not answering right now. Try again in a moment; it does not count towards your limit.
dns.nxdomain: The domain does not exist: DNS answers that there is no such name.
dns.failed: The domain could not be queried: its name servers did not answer properly.
dns.bogus: The domain's DNSSEC signature is invalid: validating resolvers reject its answers.
dns.unsigned: The domain is not signed with DNSSEC: its answers cannot be verified.
dns.no-caa: There is no CAA record: any certificate authority may issue certificates for the domain.
dns.no-spf: There is no SPF record: nothing declares which servers may send mail for the domain.
dns.no-dmarc: There is no DMARC record (_dmarc): nothing says what to do with mail that spoofs the domain.
security.part-skipped: Does not apply to this destination.
security.hop.https-downgrade: A redirect at {host} goes from https to http: from there on, traffic travels unencrypted.
security.hop.domain-change: A redirect at {host} leads to another site.
security.not-checked.reputation: The site's reputation: we do not check lists of dangerous or phishing sites.
security.not-checked.content: The page content: we do not look for phishing, malware or dangerous downloads.
